name: Grass
overview: Scripture reveals that grass, created by God on the third day, symbolizes both the beauty and brevity of life. It flourishes in the morning but withers by evening, illustrating the fleeting nature of human existence (Psalms 90:5-6). Grass is also used figuratively to describe the wicked, who are like grass on the housetops that wither before fully growing (Psalms 129:6), while God's care refreshes the saints like rain upon mown grass (Psalms 72:6). Ultimately, all flesh is likened to grass, emphasizing human frailty and the transient glory of life (Isaiah 40:6).
